     I'll let your answer be this.  Context is defined as:
         1.  Any phrase, sentence, or passage so closely connected
                to a word or words as to affect their meaning.
         2.  Something that surrounds and influences, as
                environment or circumstances.
         3.  (Obs.) The whole text of a discourse or writing.

      Since someone would probably need to be White in order to be a
      White Supremacist (or Black in order to be a Black Supremacist)
      then in order to assess that particular brand of racism we would
      need to know the environment or circumstances of the racist.
      Thereby racism is "context dependent" and exists as something
      relative rather than absolute.  Its conclusions are arbitrary.

    Done.  ISAIF doesn't use the word "indispensable."  References
  to "useful" are as follows:


 (1) 97. Constitutional rights are useful up to a point, but they
     do not serve to guarantee much more than what might be
     called the bourgeois conception of freedom.

 (2) According Corporations and government agencies, when they
     find it useful, do not hesitate to collect information about
     individuals without regard to their privacy.

 (3) Sex education is obviously useful, yet the effect of sex
     education (to the extent that it is successful) is to take
     the shaping of sexual attitudes away from the family and put
     it into the hands of the state as represented by the public
     school system.

 (4) There are many people who find it difficult or impossible to
     get work, because for intellectual or psychological reasons
     they cannot acquire the level of training necessary to make
     themselves useful in the present system.

 (5) The society may find competitiveness useful, provided that
     ways are found of directing competitiveness into channels
     that serve the needs of the system.

 (6) True Believers are a useful, perhaps a necessary, ingredient
     of any revolutionary movement.

 (7) The main reason why these values have become, so to speak,
     the official values of our society is that they are useful
     to the industrial system.

 (8) Racism is discouraged because ethnic conflicts also disrupt
     the system, and discrimination wastes the talents of
     minority-group members who could be useful to the system.

 (9) Women are encouraged to have careers because their talents
     are useful to the system and, more importantly, because by
     having regular jobs women become better integrated into the
     system and tied directly to it rather than to their
     families.

 (10) Thus it may be useful to introduce a religious element into
      the rebellion against technology, the more so because
      Western society today has no strong religious foundation.

    So TK's attitude about "usefulness" occurs as a -critique- on
  the philosophy of utilitarianism, which is defined to be:

     1.a.  (Philos.) A system that holds usefulness to be the
           end and criterion of action; especially, the doctrine
           that actions derive their moral quality from their
           usefulness as means to some end, as happiness.
     1.b.  The ethical theory, held by Jeremy Bentham, James
           Mill, and John Stuart Mill, that the greatest human
           happiness determines the highest moral good.
     2.    A similar doctrine applied to social and political
           action.
     3.    Devotion to mere material interests and aims.

     TK is not a utilitarian because the revolution of which he speaks
   is "non-political" and thereby does not satisfy (2.)  TK was not
   devoted to "mere material interests and aims" (living in poverty)
   so his philosophy of life does not satisfy (3.)  TK considers the
   manner of exploitation conducted by "Corporations and government
   agencies", "the public school system", "the present system", "the
   industrial system," "the system," or "Western society today," or
   "the borgeois conception of freedom," as -odious-, so TK regards
   "usefulness" as a despicable term of blatant manipulation of the
   freedom of others. TK's stated philosophy does not satisfy the
   definition of (1.)

     His reference to "True Believers" says they would be "useful"
   to -any- revolutionary movement.  However TK isn't talking about
   -any- revolutionary movement; he's talking specifically about a
   "non-political" revolution, which is -not- "any revolutionary
   movement."  It's quite clear from the way TK "uses" the word
   "useful" that he despises its social utilization altogether.
   People are not valued because they are "useful" to others, but
   when they are free, autonomous and independent, according to TK.
